title: Table Bloat and VACUUM
summary: A high-churn event table accumulated many dead tuples and has not been vacuumed after a large cleanup job.
incident: 10:45 — The event ingestion service deleted a large batch of obsolete rows overnight, but table maintenance did not run afterward. Query latency is trending up and pg_stat_user_tables shows a table that has never been manually vacuumed. Reclaim dead tuples safely without deleting any additional live events.
objectives: Inspect pg_stat_user_tables for dead-tuple and maintenance evidence.
Confirm the number of live rows that must be preserved.
Run appropriate VACUUM/ANALYZE maintenance on the affected table.
Verify dead tuples are cleaned up and the table remains queryable.
hints: Start with pg_stat_user_tables and look at n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_vacuum, and last_analyze.
A normal VACUUM is sufficient here; VACUUM FULL is not required for this incident.
Do not truncate or delete more rows to make the statistics look clean.

setup_sql: CREATE TABLE event_log (id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY, event_type TEXT NOT NULL, payload TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()); INSERT INTO event_log(id, event_type, payload, created_at) SELECT gs, CASE WHEN gs % 3 = 0 THEN 'checkout' WHEN gs % 3 = 1 THEN 'payment' ELSE 'session' END, repeat(md5(gs::text), 3), now() - ((gs % 7200) || ' seconds')::interval FROM generate_series(1, 20000) AS gs; DELETE FROM event_log WHERE id <= 10000; ANALYZE event_log; CREATE TABLE incident_notes (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, note TEXT NOT NULL); INSERT INTO incident_notes(note) VALUES ('The cleanup job intentionally removed 10,000 obsolete events; 10,000 live rows must remain.'), ('The table has not been vacuumed since the cleanup.'), ('Use normal online maintenance; do not delete additional live events.');

checks.name: Live events preserved
checks.feedback: Exactly 10,000 live events should remain. Do not delete additional production-style rows.

checks.name: Manual VACUUM completed
checks.sql: SELECT last_vacuum IS NOT NULL FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND relname = 'event_log'
checks.feedback: PostgreSQL still shows no manual VACUUM for event_log. Run safe online maintenance on the affected table.

checks.name: Dead tuples reclaimed
checks.sql: SELECT n_dead_tup <= 100 FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND relname = 'event_log'
checks.feedback: Too many dead tuples remain after maintenance. Confirm VACUUM completed on event_log.

checks.name: Event table remains queryable
checks.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM event_log WHERE event_type = 'checkout'
checks.feedback: The event table is not responding normally after maintenance.

evaluation.success_feedback: The event table has been vacuumed, dead tuples are reclaimed, all 10,000 live events remain, and normal queries still succeed.
